abstract: Regulation of alternative splicing (AS) is important in controlling cellular functions. More than 95% human genes are alternatively spliced and AS is regulated by close to 100 splicing factors. Line of evidences suggest that virus infections alter the AS pattern of numerous host genes. In this study we have investigated Chandipura virus (CHPV) induced alteration of host cell SR protein gene expressions and determined if these changes have any effect on apoptotic factor BCL-2 levels. CHPV is a negative stranded RNA virus which causes fever, brain encephalitis and death among young children with a case-fatality rate of 50%. Few studies were done in past to understand the roles of host factors in CHPV pathogenesis and no study was done on virus induced changes in AS. Our study showed that there is a down-regulation of SR proteins SRp55 and SRp75 expression levels significantly decreased in the CHPV infected Vero E6 cells compared to uninfected cells. For a comparison, we also looked at the levels of SRp55 and SRp75 in dengue virus (DENV) infected cells. Our results showed that SRp75 levels is unchanged whereas SRp55 levels increased in DENV infected cells. We have also determined the levels of large and small splice variants of apoptotic gene BCL-2 to find out possible correlation between the altered splicing factor expressions and virus infected cell death via apoptosis. Our data indicates that in CHPV infected cells, BCL-2 large splice variant expressions decreased as compared to uninfected cells. This is the first study of CHPV mediated alteration of splicing factor expressions and these results warrant further study with other viruses to better understand the global changes in host splicing events, cell survival, host immune response during virus infection.

summary: Chandipura virus lowers host SR splicing factors SRp55 and SRp75 and reduces large BCL-2 splice variant levels in Vero E6 cells, unlike dengue virus.
